chunks: And it is narrated from Ḥanān ibn Sadīr, who said:

Fayḍ ibn al-Mukhtār presented a rabīthā to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام. He brought it in to him while I was with him. So he looked at it and said, “This has a covering,” then he ate from it while we were watching him.

key_terms.أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abū ʿAbdillāh, Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام
key_terms.رَبِيثًا: a rabīthā, the gifted animal mentioned in the report

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith indicate about the permissibility of eating rabīthā according to Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This narration reports that Fayḍ ibn al-Mukhtār gifted a rabīthā to Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام, and the Imam ate from it after remarking that it had a covering. The report is used in the context of hunting and slaughtering, indicating permissibility through the Imam’s action.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4205 - It is narrated from Hanan ibn Sadir who said:

"Fayd ibn Al-Mukhtar gifted a rabbit (al-rabitha) to Abu Abdullah (as). He brought it to him while I was present.
Imam (as) looked at it and said: "This has a shell (skin)," and Imam (as) ate from it while we were observing.
